newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Shipley wrong on NZ superannuation scheme - Peters.
newsitem.headline: Shipley wrong on NZ superannuation scheme - Peters.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters on Tuesday rejected criticism of the retirement savings scheme by his senior cabinet colleague Jenny Shipley, saying her analysis was "dramatically wrong".
He denied the scheme amounted to privatisation of supperannuation, as Shipley said on Monday night when she launched the strongest attack on it so far from any minister.
"This is not privatisation. Since when has a government top-up been privatisation? There is a total misunderstanding here," Peters told Radio New Zealand.
Peters said the option Shipley preferred, income-tested state superannuation, would mean hundreds of thousands of people on a pension just above the poverty level.
"Her system proposes an income test...its a surtax with a vengeance. It means people who save for all they're worth, work hard to become valuable contributors, get virtually nothing.
"Anyone who has done their best to get on with life and pay taxes will get virtually nothing -- how fair is that?" he said.
Peters also denied that big costs would be run up by private fund managers who would handle investments under the proposed scheme.
He said the present super scheme was administered by public servants and it was costing billions.
"It is costing so much that this country can't go on paying for it."
Shipley told a meeting of Auckland business executives on Modnay that Peters' plan would hurt women, beneficiaries, young people and the self employed, along with the economy in general.
She called for a return to an income-tested pension as the only alternative to the "inequitable and politically unsustainable" scheme.
She called for a means-tested pension with "a universal element available to all and a tightly income tested top-up for those who have no other sources of income".
